resultText:
I found 7 bugs, all on the new Stats page (`frontend/app/pages/stats.vue`), and I saw every one happen in the running app. The findings are written to `out/findings.json`.

1. **Old results can replace new ones (high).** If you change the date range while an earlier request is still loading, the late answer overwrites the newer one. In my test, From showed 1 Jan 2026 but the table showed July–December data. It comes up in normal use: typing a year into the date field sends a request on every keystroke (years 0002, 0020, 0202, then 2024).
2. **Loading never ends if the server hangs (medium).** There is no 10-second timeout, so "Loading stats…" was still on screen after 12 seconds and would stay forever.
3. **No retry on the error state (medium).** The error message has no Retry button. To try the same range again you have to change a date or reload the page. Recovery does work once you change a date.
4. **A malformed response crashes the page (medium).** When the API returned a list as null, the page threw an uncaught TypeError. The address bar showed /stats, but the dashboard stayed on screen under an error overlay.
5. **Old summary line shown next to the error (low).** After a failed load, "5 harvests from 1 Jan…" from the previous range stays above "Could not load harvest stats."
6. **The "Stats" nav link doesn't reset the page (low).** On a custom range, clicking it changes the address to plain /stats but keeps the custom dates and data. The page ignores the address, so back and forward between ranges don't update the fields either.
7. **A blank date field quietly uses a hidden default (low).** A cleared From date silently means 1 January of this year. Combined with a To date in an earlier year, you get "The From date must be on or before the To date" even though you never set a From date. Opening a link with only a past To date shows the same error.

These checks passed:
- **Server validation:** bad dates (30 February, year 10000, text, empty, From after To) all get a 422 error, never a 500.
- **Narrow screens:** at 375 px, both pages fit without sideways scrolling, even with an 80-character plant name.
- **Odd text:** emoji, quotes and HTML in a plant's variety display as plain text.
- **Dashboard:** the top plant appears with its weight and links to Stats.

I didn't test failures during the first server-rendered load, because the browser mocks can't reach server-side requests.

To test long names and very large weights, I added a plant with two harvests through the API, then deleted all three, so the sample data is back as it was.
